Alex: Heads-up — Creston asked for a concise SLO one-pager for their onboarding + procurement packet. They specifically want uptime, latency breakdown, and an example credits calculation. Can we align on what to share?
Priya (Creston): Procurement is on a tight timeline — review next Tue. They said p99 latency they'd accept is ~500ms and target uptime 99.9% SLA. They also want a sample credit calc they can include.
Sam: We can add p50/p95/p99 and per-route latency to the customer dashboard. For credits we need to agree the measurement window (30d rolling is standard) and the formula. Suggest we stick with hosted baseline formula so procurement has a clear example.
Maya: I'll draft the one-pager template and include links to the dashboard. Can someone confirm the canonical credit formula we should show?
Alex: Baseline hosted formula: credit = ((SLA - achieved) / SLA) * committed_amount, capped at X% (we usually cap at 100% of monthly for Hosted). Dedicated/Private may be bespoke. We'll include the caveats.
Sam: Quick worked example for the one-pager: if SLA=99.9% and achieved=99.6% over 30d and commitment=$50,000 then delta=0.3% -> credit ≈ ((0.999-0.996)/0.999)*50000 ≈ $150. Snippet to paste: ```achieved=0.996
sla=0.999
credit=(sla-achieved)/sla*commitment```
SLO-bot: SLO check (auto): Creston (crst-221) 30d uptime=99.78%, p99 latency=420ms. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/crst-221/slo :information_source:
Priya (Creston): This is great. Can we also include a 2–3 sentence explainer about fallback behavior (what happens when capacity is constrained) so procurement knows how failover affects latency/consistency?
Sam: Sure — will add a short blurb: "On capacity constraints requests are routed to compatible model variants (smaller/quantized) to preserve availability; this prioritizes throughput and may increase generation time or minor quality degradation but avoids total outages."
Alex: Action items: Maya — create one-pager draft + include dashboard link; Sam — add sample calc + fallback blurb; Alex — review and send final to Priya. ETA: EOD Friday. Any objections? :thumbsup:
Priya (Creston): No objections, that timeline works. Thanks all!
